parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a wire. Refer to Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Close the switch. Measure the current I in the circuit. Include the unit. I = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: I to at least 2 decimal places and  1 A

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Place the sliding contact S at a distance d = 50.0 cm from B.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure the potential difference (p.d.) V 50 across length d of the resistance wire. Include the unit. Open the switch. V 50 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text: V to at least 1 decimal place and  3 V

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R 50 of 50.0 cm of the resistance wire using the equation R 50 = V 50 I . Include the unit. R 50 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(b)(ii)
ms.text: units V and A seen correctly used in (a) and (b)

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate r 1 , a value for the resistance per cm of the resistance wire, using the equation r 1 = R 50 d , where d = 50.0 cm. Include the unit. r 1 = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(b)(iii)
ms.text:
correct calculation of r1
unit Ω / cm

ms.text: new set of results present with r2 value within 10% of r1

parts.text: (d) A student suggests that the resistance per cm of the resistance wire is constant.

statement to match results
